newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on exports, funds, rain delays.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on exports, funds, rain delays.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on exporter demand, some fund buying and the rain delayed harvest, traders said.
"There was excellent export buying, funds bought about 150 November," a trader said. "We're covering exports to Japan and the threat of frost is still there," a trader said.
Also, rain delays in the canola harvest in some areas were supportive, sources said.
Japan bought 15,000-20,000 tonnes. Europeans were said to be looking at pricing in the January futures.
November canola rose $4.40 to $432.70, January rose $3.90 to $436. Sep-Nov spread at $5, Nov-Jan $3.50, Jan-Mar $0.50.
October flax rose $1.80 to $388.20, November up $1 to $363 on commercial, 200 Oct-Nov spread at $25. Volume was 575.
"Rain's delaying the barley harvest, there's scale down commercial buying. People are waiting for StatsCan's stocks report Tuesday," a trader said.

February western barley slipped $0.10 to $156.90. October feed wheat lost $2.60 to $205.80 and December was down $0.20 to $193.40. Spreading was the feature with the Dec-Mar spread at $0.50, Oct-Mar $13, Oct-Dec $13, sources said.
LFG bought 30 December feed peas up US$0.50 at US$211.50, traders noted. Commercials sold 25 October oats down US$1 to US$135.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
